specification.scope: Whether an x402 evidence record identifies one EIP-3009 authorization (network, asset contract, payer and nonce together), and whether a chain read of that contract identifies the Transfer log that settled it. The two answers are separate verdicts. Chain reads are modelled fields, never fetched.
specification.status: proposal of this repository, not a vendored upstream text

eip3009.used: AuthorizationUsed(authorizer, nonce) and the optional AuthorizationCanceled(authorizer, nonce) events, authorizationState(authorizer, nonce), nonces unique to the authorizer on one contract, and transferWithAuthorization requiring block time before validBefore

x402.used: the exact scheme's EIP-3009 authorization fields, settlement_pending with a broadcast transaction hash, CAIP-2 network identifiers and the v1 network names mapped to chain ids

vectors.description: case B: two payments in one transaction; payer and nonce identify the authorization, the log index names its Transfer
vectors.rationale: TKCollective's record B: payer and nonce identify which authorization was used once matched to AuthorizationUsed on the stated network, and the log index beside the transaction hash names the Transfer in the batch.

vectors.description: case C after confirmation: AuthorizationUsed read, one Transfer in the transaction, no log index needed
vectors.rationale: The log index is needed only where the transaction carries more than one transfer, as XFuel-Lab's revised wording says; with one Transfer the hash and the event suffice.

vectors.description: network alias pair: the same record with the network served as base
vectors.rationale: TKCollective's alias test: the record keeps base as served; mapped through x402's v1 table it names eip155:8453, so the answer equals the eip155:8453 twin's.

vectors.description: case A: bound by the accepted option and time only; two payments in the batch fit
vectors.rationale: TKCollective's record A: the option and time fit both payments, so the record identifies neither authorization nor transfer. Both payments settled, and that does not make settlement verified: the record names no transfer.

vectors.description: accepted option only; exactly one payment in the read fits
vectors.rationale: Decided here: the revised wording says unresolved where more than one payment fits and is silent where one does. A read covers some transactions, not every payment the option could match, so one fit in the read does not identify the authorization.

vectors.description: case B without its log index: the authorization is identified, its Transfer is not
vectors.rationale: The transaction carries two Transfer logs of the asset. EIP-3009 fixes no order between AuthorizationUsed and Transfer (the order is in its reference implementation only), so a verifier does not pair them by position; without the log index the transfer stays open.

vectors.description: the log index names the batch's other Transfer, which pays a different amount
vectors.rationale: The named log is a Transfer of the asset, but not of this authorization's value.

vectors.description: the record names a transaction; AuthorizationUsed for its nonce is in another one
vectors.rationale: The chain read places this authorization's use in another transaction.

vectors.description: case C: authorization identified; no AuthorizationUsed yet and validBefore not reached
vectors.rationale: XFuel-Lab's record C: bound to one authorization with settlement unconfirmed, not contradicted. A verifier that answers unresolved for both A and C loses the authorization C identifies.

vectors.description: case C holding the facilitator's broadcast hash (settlement_pending)
vectors.rationale: x402 v2 lets a facilitator return settlement_pending with the broadcast hash. A hash is not a settlement: the read shows the authorization unused before validBefore.

vectors.description: twin of C: unused at a finalized head whose time is past validBefore
vectors.rationale: Decided here, from EIP-3009: transferWithAuthorization requires block time before validBefore, so once a finalized head is past it with the authorization unused, the authorization can never settle. Never settled, not pending. The head's time is the clock, not the verifier's.

vectors.description: twin of C: past validBefore at the head, but the head is not finalized
vectors.rationale: A head that is not final can be replaced by blocks timed before validBefore that carry the authorization, so the answer stays pending.

vectors.description: the read shows AuthorizationCanceled for the payer and nonce
vectors.rationale: EIP-3009's optional cancelAuthorization marks the nonce used without a transfer.

vectors.description: authorizationState is true, but the read carries no AuthorizationUsed log
vectors.rationale: The nonce is spent somewhere; without the event the transaction and its Transfer are unknown.

vectors.description: read-failed half of the pair: the source was unavailable
vectors.rationale: XFuel-Lab asked to keep the reason: source unavailable here, not found in c-authorization-not-yet-used. Both are indeterminate and neither counts against the record.

vectors.description: an offline run: no chain read was made
vectors.rationale: The authorization is identified from the record alone; settlement was not evaluated, which is visible and is not a failure.

vectors.description: the read is of eip155:84532; the record is bound to eip155:8453
vectors.rationale: A read of another chain says nothing about this authorization.

vectors.description: the single Transfer after AuthorizationUsed credits another address than payTo
vectors.rationale: The transfer the read identifies is not this authorization's terms.

vectors.description: the network is served as base-mainnet, which no mapping names
vectors.rationale: TKCollective's rule: with an unknown identifier the network comparison stays unresolved, so the authorization's scope is not established.

vectors.description: the binding names another nonce than the authorization the record carries
vectors.rationale: The record contradicts itself about which authorization binds it.

vectors.description: the binding names payer and nonce but no asset contract
vectors.rationale: An EIP-3009 nonce is unique to its authorizer on one contract, so payer and nonce without the asset and network do not identify one authorization.
